subject.title: Org owners cannot roll back latest after accidental higher-version skill publish

question: Should organization publishers receive an explicit auditable rollback/repoint operation for `latest`, or should recovery remain limited to publishing a new higher version?
rationale: Current deletion behavior intentionally protects the active distribution target, but the issue demonstrates that strict semver promotion leaves no self-service recovery when an organization publishes on the wrong higher version line. The choice affects package trust, installer expectations, and the permanent publisher API contract.

options.title: Add guarded latest rollback
options.body: Authorize publisher owners through the existing organization-role checks to repoint `latest` only to an existing public, approved version, with explicit confirmation and an audit record.

options.title: Require a forward replacement
options.body: Keep `latest` monotonic and require affected publishers to publish a new higher corrective version, preserving the current installer semantics.

options.title: Offer moderated recovery only
options.body: Keep the CLI/API unchanged and handle exceptional tag corrections through staff moderation while product policy is refined.

recommendation.title: Add guarded latest rollback
recommendation.body: Authorize publisher owners through the existing organization-role checks to repoint `latest` only to an existing public, approved version, with explicit confirmation and an audit record.

likelyOwner.reason: The current tag behavior appears to originate in the recent skill-version publishing work they authored.
